instructions: There are NINE questions in this paper.

questions.text: Answer any seven of the following :

sub_questions.text: Evolutionary life cycle model is ideally suited for development of very small software products typically requiring a few month of development effort. Mark either True of False. Justify your answer.

An SRS document normally contains : (i) Functional requirements of the system, (ii) Module structure, (iii) Configuration management plan, (iv) Non-functional requirements of the system, (v) Constraints on the system.
A module is said to have logical cohesion, if
options: it performs a set of tasks that relate to each other very loosely.
all the functions of the module are executed within the same time span.
all elements of the module perform similar operations, e.g. error handling, data input, data output etc.

sub_questions.text: What is the importance of constructing DFDs in the context of a good software design?
Which diagrams in UML capture the behavioural view of the system?
Differentiate between structured analysis and structured design.

questions.text: Discuss in detail the different phases of a classical waterfall model. What is the advantage of using prototype software development model instead of waterfall model?

sub_questions.text: What are the components of the standard structure for software requirements document? Explain in detail.

Briefly describe the activities of software configuration management.

questions.text: What is meant by ISO 9000 certification? Discuss about the shortcomings of ISO 9000 certification process? What are the salient features of ISO 9001 certification? Why is it important for a software development organization to obtain ISO 9001 certification.
What is cyclomatic complexity? Explain in detail how cyclomatic complexity can be computed.

sub_questions.text: Elaborate on the challenges involved in risk management.
